domain_restrictions: Each entry s_i is either plus 1 or minus 1.
The sequence a is a permutation of the set {1 through n}, so every number from 1 through n appears exactly once.
For j = 1, the left_count definition uses the base value 1.
For j greater than or equal to 2, left_count(j) counts permutations of 1 through j minus 1, and the sign conditions run over i from 1 to j minus 2; this range is empty when j = 2.
For j = n, the right_count definition uses the base value 1.

For j less than or equal to n minus 1, right_count(j) counts permutations of 1 through n minus j, and the sign conditions run over i from 1 to n minus j minus 1; this range is empty when j = n minus 1.
The valley set V(s) is a subset of 1 through n and is determined only by the local sign pattern around each index.
The binomial coefficient uses n minus 1 choose j minus 1, so j must lie between 1 and n inclusive.
semantic_sketch_json.normalized_claim: For every integer n at least 2 and every sign sequence s of length n minus 1 with entries plus 1 or minus 1, the number of permutations of 1 through n whose adjacent differences match the signs in s equals the sum over all valley positions j of the product of three factors: the binomial coefficient n minus 1 choose j minus 1, the number of valid left permutations up to j, and the number of valid right permutations from j onward.
quantifier_order: Assume n is an integer with n at least 2.
Assume s is a sign sequence of length n minus 1, with each entry equal to plus 1 or minus 1.
Define F(s) as the number of permutations a of 1 through n such that for every i from 1 to n minus 1, the sign condition s_i times the difference a_{i+1} minus a_i is positive.
Define V(s) by endpoint rules at 1 and n and by the interior rule for each j between 2 and n minus 1.

For each j in V(s), define left_count(j) by a base case at j = 1 and otherwise by counting permutations b of 1 through j minus 1 satisfying the analogous sign conditions for indices 1 through j minus 2.

For each j in V(s), define right_count(j) by a base case at j = n and otherwise by counting permutations c of 1 through n minus j satisfying the analogous sign conditions for indices j plus 1 through n minus 1.
Claim that F(s) equals the sum over j in V(s) of binomial n minus 1 choose j minus 1 times left_count(j) times right_count(j).

witness_dependencies: The counted permutation a in F(s) depends only on the full sign sequence s.
The set V(s) depends only on s.
For each j in V(s), left_count(j) depends on j and on the prefix of s needed to evaluate the sign conditions up to index j minus 2.
For each j in V(s), right_count(j) depends on j and on the suffix of s needed to evaluate the sign conditions from index j plus 1 onward.
The witness permutation b for left_count(j) is local to the interval 1 through j minus 1 and does not depend on any choices outside that interval.
The witness permutation c for right_count(j) is local to the interval 1 through n minus j and does not depend on any choices outside that interval.
No existential witness is shared across different j values in the sum.

statement_nl: Let n be an integer with n at least 2, and let s=(s_1,...,s_{n-1}) be a sign sequence with each s_i equal to plus 1 or minus 1. Let F(s) be the number of permutations a=(a_1,...,a_n) of {1,...,n} such that s_i(a_{i+1}-a_i) > 0 for every i=1,...,n-1. Define the valley set V(s) subset of {1,...,n} by: 1 belongs to V(s) exactly when s_1 = plus 1; n belongs to V(s) exactly when s_{n-1} = minus 1; and for 2 <= j <= n-1, j belongs to V(s) exactly when s_{j-1} = minus 1 and s_j = plus 1. For each j in V(s), define left_count(j) as follows: if j=1 then left_count(j)=1; if j>=2 then left_count(j) is the number of permutations b=(b_1,...,b_{j-1}) of {1,...,j-1} satisfying s_i(b_{i+1}-b_i) > 0 for every i=1,...,j-2. Define right_count(j) as follows: if j=n then right_count(j)=1; if j<=n-1 then right_count(j) is the number of permutations c=(c_1,...,c_{n-j}) of {1,...,n-j} satisfying s_{j+i}(c_{i+1}-c_i) > 0 for every i=1,...,n-j-1. Then F(s) = sum over j in V(s) of binomial(n-1,j-1) times left_count(j) times right_count(j).
